ground_truth: Final confirmed diagnosis: Primary (PLA2R-associated) membranous nephropathy that initially mimicked resolving post-infectious/post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. The first renal biopsy showed widespread foot-process effacement with subepithelial "hump"-type deposits and granular IgG/C3 positivity — a picture classically read as resolving post-infectious GN — and the patient had a recent UTI treated with amoxicillin, reinforcing that misleading interpretation. The load-bearing discriminator was a markedly elevated serum anti-PLA2R antibody (686 RU/mL; normal <14), which is specific for primary membranous nephropathy and discordant with a post-infectious diagnosis. How confirmed: a REPEAT renal biopsy four weeks later showed histology consistent with membranous nephropathy, aligning tissue findings with the strongly positive PLA2R serology. Correct disposition/treatment: recognize the serology–histology discordance and re-biopsy rather than waiting for spontaneous resolution; treat as primary membranous nephropathy with immunosuppression — oral prednisolone (weaning regimen) plus rituximab (two infusions two weeks apart), alongside supportive nephrotic management (high-dose IV furosemide up to 320 mg/24h with metolazone, albumin infusions, fluid restriction, anticoagulation given thrombotic risk).
